title: Majestic Combination: Test the Relative Pin
summary: Fork king and queen, then check the legal pawn capture and the actual rook-versus-pawns conversion instead of assuming the queen gain ends the calculation.

nodes.question: How does the rook prepare a fork even when the pawn can capture?
nodes.explanation: Ra7+ forces Kb4 and places the rook behind the d7 blocker. Nc6+ then forks king and queen; dxc6 remains legal, but exposes Qe7 to the rook.

branches.title: Independent defense: the pinned pawn captures legally
commentary: Begin after Ka3 at123 seconds with White Kc2/Rb7/Nd4 against Ka3/Qe7/d7/d6/e6/h7. The king route has prepared a change from chasing checks to a concrete fork.
Ra7+ checks on the a-file and lines the rook up with Qe7 behind d7. The white king and knight cover the lower king escapes.
Kb4 is the only legal answer to the rook check. White now has the nine-piece fork setup shown in native30/31.
Nc6+ checks b4 and attacks Qe7. White threatens to collect the queen after a king move.
dxc6 is a legal answer to check. The d7 pawn captures the knight; the pin is to a queen, not to Black’s king, so chess rules do not prohibit it.
Rxe7 captures the exposed queen along the seventh rank. White Kc2/Re7 faces Kb4/c6/d6/e6/h7: the complete seven-piece ending is an exact White win, not a material-count assumption.

branches.title: Source king reply, then an independent pawn collection
commentary: Begin after Ka3 at123 seconds with White Kc2/Rb7/Nd4 against Ka3/Qe7/d7/d6/e6/h7. The king route has prepared a change from chasing checks to a concrete fork.
Ra7+ checks on the a-file and lines the rook up with Qe7 behind d7. The white king and knight cover the lower king escapes.
Kb4 is the only legal answer to the rook check. White now has the nine-piece fork setup shown in native30/31.
Nc6+ forks king and queen while the rook attacks through the d7 blocker.
Kc5 answers the check by moving the king. The queen remains attacked by Nc6.
Nxe7 takes the queen and leaves eight pieces. All d7/d6/e6/h7 pawns remain, so a complete conversion proof is still required.
h6 is an independent representative pawn reply. It does not remove the d7 blocker from the rook’s path.
Rxd7 collects that pawn. White Kc2/Rd7/Ne7 faces Kc5/d6/e6/h6: seven complete pieces and an exact White win.

exercises.prompt: Why is dxc6 legal despite the pin?
exercises.answer: Moving the pawn exposes the queen rather than the king. It is a relative pin; Black may sacrifice its queen, and the resulting ending must be checked.

exercises.prompt: Why continue after winning the queen?
exercises.answer: Nxe7 leaves eight pieces, including four black pawns. The finite proof checks every Black reply through exact supported winning endings; the displayed h6/Rxd7 is one representative continuation.
